title: Correctness of the Multiplication Computation
statement: Let $x,a,b,c$ be Boolean words such that $x=\langle a,\langle b,c\rangle\rangle$, and let $v$ assign a natural number to each of thirteen registers. Suppose every register value is at most $4(|x|+1)$, and the register values satisfy $v(1)=|x|$, $v(2)=2|a|+2$, $v(3)=2|a|+2+2|b|+2$, $v(4)=2|a|$, $v(5)=2|a|+2+2|b|$, $v(6)=|a|+|b|$, and $v(7)=v(11)=v(12)=0$. Starting in the canonicality-test state for field $0$, with register values $v$ and no answer recorded, the multiplication procedure eventually halts with the Boolean answer indicating whether $x$ belongs to the multiplication language.
hypotheses_covered: every register value is at most $4(|x|+1)$
initial state is canonicality-test for field $0$
replaced:
Let $x,a,b,c$ be bit strings with $x=\langle a,\langle b,c\rangle\rangle$, and let $v$
assign a natural-number register value to each of thirteen registers. Suppose every
register value is at most $4(|x|+1)$, and the initial register values satisfy $v_1=|x|$,
$v_2=2|a|+2$, $v_3=2|a|+2+2|b|+2$, $v_4=2|a|$, $v_5=2|a|+2+2|b|$, $v_6=|a|+|b|$, and
$v_7=v_{11}=v_{12}=0$. Starting in the canonicality-check state with these registers and
no answer yet, the multiplication machine halts with the Boolean answer indicating
whether $x$ belongs to the binary multiplication language; at every earlier step its
configuration satisfies the machine's prescribed precondition and all register values
remain at most $4(|x|+1)$.
